newsitem.title: USA: Icelandic Magnesium says smelter project viable.
newsitem.headline: Icelandic Magnesium says smelter project viable.

text.p: Icelandic Magnesium Co., a project company formed last year, said a feasibility study has confirmed the technical viability of a 50,000 tonnes per year primary magnesium smelter in Iceland.

"The production process has been tailored to the unique Icelandic availability of low cost, long term geothermal steam and hydro power, and is based on unlimited availability of sea water and shell sand," IMC said in a statement.
Project partners are headed by Preussag group member, Salzgitter Anlegenbau, who are the general contractor and offering a turnkey contract.
The supplier of the core know-how of electrolytic cell technology and dehydration is the Russian/Ukrainian Consortium Magniy.
"The selected concept of proven technology does not require piloting and will meet Icelandic environmental demands," the IMC statement said.
All the chlorine in the process will be recycled in a closed circuit.

Work on engineering, including the infrastructure and port facilities, together with environmental studies are in advanced stages so that permitting and construction of the plant can begin immediately after the go-ahead decision planned for December 1997/January 1998.
Amalgamet Canada, part of Preussag, is marketing the output.

Following board meetings late last week, IMC shareholders approved raising capital to further optimize project configuration and design by examining cost saving options which have been identified, finalize strategic alliances with long term clients, and continue discussions with potential partners and investors.
With current world primary magnesium production at about 280,000 tonnes, the new smelter will represent a significant addition to capacity.
Iceland's Sudurnes Regional Heating Corp is also part of the IMC consortium.
